Kubernetes accepts all traffic to and from a pod until some NetworkPolicy selects it for that direction. This report lists the workloads where that is still the case, and flags the ones that were seen talking to public addresses.

```bash
netractl insights netpol-coverage [--namespace NS] [--window 24h] [--all] [--limit 200]
```

`GET /api/v1/insights/netpol-coverage` (viewer role; a namespace-scoped principal lists only its own namespaces). MCP: `netra_insights_netpol_coverage`. Console: **Policy Coverage**.

Read-only: it lists pods and NetworkPolicies and reads the flow history. It creates, changes and suggests no policy.

## Permission

The controller's ClusterRole needs `get` and `list` on `networking.k8s.io` `networkpolicies`. The Helm chart and `deploy/rbac.yaml` grant it from 0.33.0. If you manage RBAC yourself and upgrade only the image, the endpoint answers 502 naming the missing permission; it never reports everything as open because a list failed.

## What each state means

Per direction, for each pod, following the upstream rules (`policyTypes` defaults to Ingress, plus Egress when the policy has egress rules; selectors apply within the policy's namespace; rules of all selecting policies are a union):

| Count | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `open` | No policy selects the pod for this direction |
| `allowAll` | Selected, but some rule has neither peers nor ports, so everything is allowed |
| `restricted` | Selected, and no rule allows everything |
| `restrictedButAnyAddress` | Restricted, but a rule still names `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`, or limits only ports |

A workload is `uncovered` when every pod is unrestricted (`open` or `allowAll`) in both directions, `partial` when some pod is unrestricted in some direction, and `covered` otherwise. Covered rows are listed only with `--all`. `attention` marks an unrestricted direction that was seen with a public peer in the flow window. `namespacesWithoutPolicy` lists namespaces that run pods and have no NetworkPolicy at all.

## Limits

- Only `networking.k8s.io/v1` NetworkPolicy. CiliumNetworkPolicy, CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy, Calico policies, AdminNetworkPolicy and Netra's own deny rules are not counted, so a workload shown open may be restricted by one of them.
- Whether the CNI enforces NetworkPolicy is not checked.
- Restricted means isolated, not tight. This is not a connectivity simulation and does not say which observed flows a rule would drop.
- `hostNetwork` pods are excluded (Kubernetes leaves their policy behaviour undefined); finished pods are not counted.
- Workloads are named by the controlling owner (a Deployment's pods show their ReplicaSet), as elsewhere in Netra.
- Public traffic is joined from flow history by namespace and pod, or workload name for pods that have since been replaced. No traffic shown is not proof there was none.
- Window 1m up to the flow retention (at most 14 days); at most 1000 rows.

## Validation

`go test ./internal/netpolcoverage ./internal/api -run 'Isolation|Egress|Deny|Selector|Public|Coverage'` covers the `policyTypes` defaults, default-deny and allow-all rules, the union of policies, every selector operator, hostNetwork exclusion, the flow join, namespace scoping (only the allowed namespaces are listed) and a missing permission. `web/src/lib/netpolCoverage.test.ts` covers the console helpers. It has not been run against a live cluster's API server.
